question: Enough to change the war, yes or no?

lines.text: Britain is giving Ukraine another ten billion pounds, its biggest package ever.
Chancellor John Healey announced it in today's Budget, after a call with Zelensky.
Five hundred million pounds of it goes on Ukraine's air defences this winter.
Another seven billion pounds is economic support, spread over three years.
Up to five and a half billion of that is World Bank guarantees.
And UK Export Finance gets three billion pounds more, mainly for military support.
Prime Minister Andy Burnham says this is the largest ever package of funding for Ukraine from the UK.

scene.quote: This is the largest ever package of funding for Ukraine from the UK

lines.text: Healey told MPs that Zelensky's reply on the call was: you've made my day.

scene.who: Zelensky, as told by John Healey

lines.text: The UK government says its total commitment to Ukraine now reaches thirty five billion pounds.
Sixteen billion of that is military support, and up to twelve point six billion is not.
Healey says Britain will keep raising sanctions on Russia to push it towards talks.
It lands in the fifth year of the war, as Ukraine heads into another winter.
Britain has now pledged thirty five billion pounds. Enough to change the war, yes or no?

caption: UK, Ukraine, Healey Budget: Britain is giving Ukraine another £10 billion, the biggest UK package ever, with £500 million for air defences this winter. The government says its total for Ukraine now reaches £35 billion. Enough to change the war, yes or no?
notes_full: First reported 28 Oct 2026: Reuters 13:57 UTC (Healey to MPs in the Budget), GOV.UK call readout and package release same afternoon; about 6h old at render

Breakdown per GOV.UK: £500m air defence, £7bn economic over 3 years (up to £5.5bn World Bank guarantees), £3bn more UKEF capacity; total commitment £35bn (£16bn military, up to £12.6bn non-military, £6.5bn export finance)
Reuters notes the £7bn + £3bn split already totals £10bn; £500m military described separately. Script keeps each figure attributed
Left out: 3% defence target debate (domestic politics), Kremlin reaction
Removal-risk: aid announcement and attributed statements; no death toll; no future-attack framing; neutral either/or
